hypotheses_tested: H1 (obligation 1 — is r7's 121-char line actually gone, and is the docblock now wholly within printWidth 100?): REJECTED as a defect. `awk 'length>100'` over the whole file reports zero lines over 100 anywhere in lines 1-114; the module docblock (now lines 1-95, terminating at the sole top-level ` */` at line 95) is entirely <=100. The r7-era file recovered from `jj op log` operation 2b57520e0aab has exactly the two long lines r7 described (line 31 at 121 chars, line 114 at 101), which confirms I recovered the right revision to compare against. The 101-char one-line docblock r7 noted at line 114 is now at line 115 — it moved because the rewrap added one net line, its content is untouched, and it is one of the pre-existing >100 lines r1-r7 never flagged, not a regression.

H2 (obligation 1, second half — did the rewrap silently alter a factual claim while reflowing?): REJECTED, by the strongest available evidence rather than by reading. I normalised both the r7-era and current docblocks to a whitespace-independent word stream (strip the leading ' *' comment gutter, collapse all runs of space/newline to one token per line) and diffed them: 1144 tokens on each side, `diff` reports no difference at all. The rewrap therefore changed line breaks and nothing else — not a word, not a punctuation mark, not a backtick. r7's minor described the offending line as ' * mid-inflate rather than trusted. This also removes the second parser entirely: fflate's `Unzip` push API walks *local*'; the current text carries that same sentence verbatim across lines 31-34, broken after "fflate's" instead of after "*local*". (r7's suggested fix was to break one word earlier, after "second parser entirely:"; the author broke one word later. Same effect, both under 100 — not a finding.)

H3 (obligation 2 — is the diff since r7 again comment-only, or did a code token ride along?): REJECTED as a risk, proven two independent ways, the same method r7 used. (a) Structural: the leading module docblock is the only region touched, so I stripped it from both revisions at the first top-level ` */` and ran `cmp` on the remainders — the post-docblock bytes are byte-for-byte identical between the r7-era file and the current one. Zero code tokens changed. (b) Line-level: `diff` of the two docblocks shows exactly one hunk, `31,33c31,34`, i.e. three ' * ' comment lines replaced by four ' * ' comment lines, and every line on both sides of that hunk begins with ' * '. (The apparent second hunk `95d95` is an artifact of my fixed head -95 window — the r7 docblock ends at line 94, so the window swept up the blank line following its terminator. Both files have exactly one blank line between ` */` and the first import.) File length went 1143 -> 1144, consistent with a 3->4 line rewrap and nothing else.

H4 (the check the round specifically asked for — does the rewrapped sentence still correctly describe the single-parser design, verified against the actual code rather than against the prose?): REJECTED as drift; the claim is accurate. The sentence asserts the module 'removes the second parser entirely' because fflate's `Unzip` push API walks *local* headers rather than the central directory the module validates. The import at store.ts:100 is `import { Inflate, strFromU8, strToU8, zipSync, type Zippable } from 'fflate'` — `Unzip` and `unzipSync` are imported nowhere and appear nowhere in the file outside comment text (grep confirms: the only `Unzip` occurrences are line 32 and the `UnzipFileInfo` type reference in a comment at line 295). `extractMembers` (store.ts:637) takes `members: readonly CentralEntry[]` from the module's own validated scan and walks them in a single `for (const entry of members)` loop, resolving each member's bytes via `memberDataRange` at the scan-validated offset and inflating it through the streaming `Inflate` constructed at store.ts:601. So 'our own validated central-directory scan, one member at a time' and 'reading drives fflate's streaming `Inflate` itself' both match the code exactly, and the write side's `zipSync` claim matches store.ts:1085.

H5 (NEW, fresh-eyes — did the reflow split a markdown/JSDoc code span across a line boundary, which would mis-render in editor hover even though the prose is unchanged?): REJECTED. This is the realistic failure mode of a hand-rewrap that H2's word-stream check cannot see, because moving a break into the middle of a `code span` preserves every token. I counted backticks per line across the whole docblock (lines 1-95) and every line has an even count — no span opens on one line and closes on the next. Specifically, the moved span is intact: line 31 ends '...second parser entirely: fflate's' and line 32 opens '`Unzip` push API walks *local* headers', with both backticks on line 32. The `*local*` emphasis pair is likewise wholly on line 32.

H6 (NEW, fresh-eyes — is the ragged short line at store.ts:56 ('...not merely the total. Both') a leftover from *this* rewrap, i.e. a fresh half-finished paragraph of the same class r6 flagged?): REJECTED — it is pre-existing and untouched. I compared lines 54-58 across the r6-era revision (op dc941e3d3f6b), the r7-era revision (2b57520e0aab) and the current file: the short line is present and character-identical in all three, and it sits far outside the single 31,33c31,34 hunk this round's edit produced. Two prior fresh-eyes rounds read this docblock closely and did not raise it. Recording it here as explicitly considered and deliberately not raised: it is a cosmetic wrap artifact in a comment, not a defect, and not a regression from the change under review. Raising it would be re-litigating settled cosmetics.

H7 (NEW, fresh-eyes — did adding a line to the docblock detach it from the module or break anything line-sensitive?): REJECTED. The docblock still terminates at a single top-level ` */` (line 95) followed by one blank line and then the import block starting at line 97, so it remains the module docblock; there is no stray `*/` inside it. Everything downstream shifted by exactly one line, and nothing depends on that: my own typecheck run is clean (which would fail on any comment-nesting mistake), lint is clean, and all 184 tests pass, so no test, snapshot, or lint suppression is anchored to a store.ts line number.

notes.summary: Round-8 confirmation of a rewrap of one comment paragraph. All three obligations check out. (1) r7's minor is fixed: no line in the module docblock exceeds 100 characters, and the docblock is now entirely within the repo's printWidth 100. (2) No factual claim moved — normalising both revisions' docblocks to a whitespace-independent word stream gives 1144 identical tokens with a zero-length diff, so the edit changed line breaks and literally nothing else; I additionally confirmed no code span was split across the new break. (3) The delta is provably comment-only: stripping the docblock leaves bytes that are byte-for-byte identical to the r7-era file, and the sole diff hunk replaces three ' * ' lines with four. On fresh eyes I re-verified the rewrapped sentence against the code it describes — `Unzip` is imported nowhere, `extractMembers` walks the module's own validated central-directory entries one at a time through a single streaming `Inflate`, so the single-parser claim is true — and confirmed the ragged short line at line 56 predates r6 and is untouched here. My own pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck and pnpm test are all green at 184/184. Zero blockers, zero majors, zero minors. Ship it; there is nothing left to confirm in another round.
